issues.why: Job 1: run timing is partially unavailable at the demonstrated window width.
issues.fix: Constrain the app to its container with border-box sizing, allow header groups to wrap, and move elapsed time and ETA onto a second line when they cannot fit without clipping.

issues.element: pass-rate values, '1.00× 99%' and '0.63× 62%'
issues.problem: Ratios receive more emphasis than the actual pass rates, adding a translation step to the primary comparison.
issues.why: Job 2: users must look past normalized values to find which arm won and its percentage-point advantage.
issues.fix: Make 99% and 62% the primary values, show '+37pp vs baseline' beneath trial, and move optional ratios to secondary text for time and cost only.

issues.element: theme toggle, 'Light theme'
issues.problem: The light-theme frame labels its toggle 'Light theme' even though the control should name the destination theme.
issues.why: This makes the toggle's next action ambiguous.
issues.fix: Bind the visible label to the active theme: show 'Dark theme' in light mode and 'Light theme' in dark mode.

Q1.why: For 2–4 arms, columns keep each metric on one comparison row and preserve the matrix's arm order. B-alt spreads metrics across a wider table, clips the cost column in the supplied frame, and makes users decode ratios before comparing actual pass rates.

top_three: Unify progress units, pooled rates and proportional bars across the matrix, hover cards, drawer and leaderboard.
Expose explicit live problem counts and provisional arm-wide rates so failures, quiet agents and the current leader are visible without searching.
Complete phone diagnosis: fix pinned-column bleed, restore sample navigation and make recent output fully readable.

output.unparsed_raw: I have the frames and the design system; next I’ll confirm the specific misreads in the matrix, drawer, leaderboard, and phone layouts before writing the critique.

issues.element: phone sheet status line "FAIL · 5/9 assertions"
issues.problem: "FAIL · 5/9 assertions" is the passed count — the caption under it says "4 failed · 5 passed" — so the headline reads as five failures.
issues.why: Job 3: the number you open a cell to read is the wrong failure count; frame C's drawer does the same ("FAIL · 6/9 assertions" beside "3 failed · 6 passed").
issues.fix: Render status as "FAIL · 4 of 9 assertions failed", using the failed count, the word "failed", and the total, from the same source as the "[ assertions · 4 failed · 5 passed ]" caption. Never put a pass fraction after FAIL.

issues.element: hover card on opencode × gemini-hack-days, "94%" and the three sample rows
issues.problem: The card says "94% · 17 of 18 checks passed" but the rows are × 9/10, error, and ✓ 10/10, which is 19 of 20 graded checks, not 17 of 18.
issues.why: Job 3: the hover card is where a problem cell is explained, and the headline disagrees with its own rows, so neither number can be trusted.
issues.fix: Compute the percent and "N of M checks passed" only from the graded rows shown in the card, excluding the errored sample, and write each fail row as "✗ 9/10 passed" so the mark is not read as 9 failures.

issues.element: phone run summary "27/31 passed · 4 running"
issues.problem: The summary says 27/31 passed and 4 running, and drops the 4 failed cells the desktop tally shows for this same run.
issues.why: Job 1: the line you read first on the phone makes a run with failures look healthy, so failing cells are not visible at a glance.
issues.fix: Use the desktop tally buckets and omit only zeros: "27 passed · 4 failed · 4 running · 31 of 78 finished". Do not show a passed/finished fraction.

issues.element: delegating-to-codex group bars under "57% · 4/15" and "100% · 3/15"
issues.problem: The baseline bar is a short sliver under a 57% label, and the trial bar is far short of full under a 100% label, so neither matches its rate or its finished fraction.
issues.why: Job 1: those bars are how you compare arms while the run is live, and here they read as barely started versus partly done.
issues.fix: Set each live group bar's width to the same pass rate printed above it (57% and 100% of the track) and paint it accent. If the arm is n/a or not run, leave the track empty.

issues.element: phone summary "15/69 passed · 1 timed out · 1 errored · 4 running" under "60% 70 of 117 finished"
issues.problem: "15/69 passed" cannot be reconciled with "70 of 117 finished" or with 60%, so the two progress readouts describe different totals.
issues.why: Job 1: on a 117-cell phone run you cannot tell how far along it is or how many cells have actually failed.
issues.fix: Use one formula: percent = finished cells / total cells, and list non-zero buckets that sum to that total ("N passed · N failed · 1 timed out · 1 errored · 4 running · N waiting"). Remove the 15/69 fraction.

issues.element: four-arm phone matrix headers "bare", "claude-code", "codex" and the core-data-model rate row
issues.problem: All four arm columns are squeezed into the 390px card, so headers, sample boxes and rates overlap and cannot be read.
issues.why: Job 1: a four-arm run is a normal case, and on the phone you cannot see which arm is failing.
issues.fix: Pin the eval-id column at 104px and lock each arm column at 112px inside a matrix-only horizontal scroller, two arms visible, with a persistent "arms 1–2 of 4" label and a right-edge fade. Never shrink columns to fit four arms.

issues.element: accent ring on the trial codex-logged-out cell labeled "100%"
issues.problem: The only accent ring is on the passing trial cell, while the pointer, hover ground and hover card all belong to the failing baseline cell.
issues.why: Job 1 and job 3: orange is the page's focal color, so the eye lands on the healthy cell instead of the failure being inspected.
issues.fix: Draw the accent ring only on the selected or focused cell, and only when that cell is the one the card or drawer describes. Hover changes the cell ground only and must not add a ring.

issues.element: leaderboard median-time trial cell "39.0s" / "1.53× best"
issues.problem: The word "best" sits on the slower arm as "1.53× best", and the same pattern is on first output and cost.
issues.why: Job 2: this tab exists to show which arm won, and "best" on the losing value credits the wrong arm.
issues.fix: Keep "◆" and the word "best" only on the winning value. On the other arm show the absolute value plus "1.53× baseline", with no "best".

issues.element: finished-run header "62/77 passed · 1 errored"
issues.problem: The phone header says 62/77 passed and mentions one error, omitting the 15 failed cells the desktop tally shows for the same run.
issues.why: Job 2: before the per-arm bars, the finished run looks clean, so the size of the loss is hidden.
issues.fix: Match the desktop finished tally exactly: "62 passed · 15 failed · 1 errored". Leave per-arm pass rates to the card below.

issues.element: not-triggers baseline summary "n/a · 12/12" with a full bar, and trial "routed 12/12 · 12/12"
issues.problem: An n/a arm draws a full summary bar, and the other arm is labeled "routed", which is not a pass rate, n/a, or not-run.
issues.why: Job 1: a skipped arm looks finished and successful, and "routed" is not in the legend, so a scoping skip can be read as a win.
issues.fix: If an arm has no scored checks, label it "n/a" or "not run", show only slashed or empty boxes, and leave the summary track empty. Remove the word "routed".

issues.element: alternative leaderboard, trial row "◆ 1.00× 99% best" and "1.53× 39.0s"
issues.problem: "1.00×" means the winner for both a higher-is-better rate and a lower-is-better time, and the cost column is clipped off the right edge.
issues.why: Job 2: a ratio above 1 looks like a win on time and cost, and the clipped column hides a metric you need to compare.
issues.fix: Do not ship ratio-to-best rows for 2–4 arms. If a row layout is kept for more than four arms, label each metric "higher is better" or "lower is better", show absolute values, and scroll the table instead of clipping it.

issues.element: triggers trial summary "- · 0/12", and the leaderboard skill-triggered "—" on frame B
issues.problem: An em dash means not started here, skill not run on the leaderboard, and every sample errored in frame E and in the spec.
issues.why: Job 1 and job 2: a dash on a live group can be read as a crash, and a dash on the leaderboard can be read as a scored zero.
issues.fix: Use words: "0/12" while nothing has finished, "not run" when the arm skipped the metric (as D2 already does), and reserve "—" for denominator 0 after errors, with the error boxes beside it.

issues.element: phone eval-id labels "plan-...ndings", "plan-...t-task", "codex...ed-out"
issues.problem: Ids are truncated from the end, so several rows collapse to the same "plan-..." prefix and cannot be told apart.
issues.why: Job 1 and job 3: on the phone the eval name is what you tap, and these labels no longer identify the failing row.
issues.fix: In the 104px pinned column, keep the leaf id and ellipsize the front ("…judges-findings", "…logged-out"), one line, no mid-word cut.

issues.element: phone sample boxes on the plan-implement-task row
issues.problem: At 10px the running dot and the quiet bar are both a warm-colored ring, so a stuck agent is not distinct from a working one.
issues.why: Job 1: quiet is the stuck state to spot during a run, and the phone hides the duration label that would name it, leaving color as the only signal.
issues.fix: On phone, fill the quiet box with the warn color and keep running as an accent ring with a dot, so they differ by fill versus stroke. Put "quiet" in the cell's accessible name.

issues.element: theme toggle labeled "Light theme"
issues.problem: On the light-theme page the toggle still says "Light theme", which is the theme already showing, not the one it switches to.
issues.why: The control no longer says what it will do, so returning to the default dark theme is a guess.
issues.fix: Label the button with the destination theme: "Dark theme" when the page is light, "Light theme" when it is dark, and keep aria-pressed in sync.

Q1.why: For 2–4 arms, arms as columns keep one metric per row so you compare two to four aligned numbers in matrix order. The row alternative encodes every value as a ratio whose direction flips by metric (1.00× wins on both pass rate and time), repeats "best" on losing cells, and clips the cost column.

top_three: Make FAIL lines, hover headlines and phone summaries use one failed/passed count, in words ("FAIL · 4 of 9 assertions failed", "27 passed · 4 failed"), never a pass fraction after FAIL.
Drive group bars and phone tallies from the same buckets as the counter, to scale, and stop drawing a full bar or the word "routed" for n/a.
On phone, scroll four arms at a fixed 112px column with the leaf eval id pinned; on desktop, put the accent ring only on the cell the card or drawer describes.
